intro: From a `.16` file to pixels: expand the LZW stream, find the records, read each record's size, unpack the pixels, then look up the colours. Every number below comes from rules GFX-0001 to GFX-0008; the build recomputes the archive offsets and checks them against those rules.
pipeline_notes: `WD.BIT`, `IBM.CH`, `RUNES.CH` and `BRITISH.PTH` are stored directly: skip step 2.
`ITEMS` and `MON` archives pair each image with a 1-bit mask.

blocks.text: One complete file has been checked: expanding the shipped `TILES.16` with this model reproduces its source sheets byte for byte. Every stream transition, the full-dictionary case, trailing padding and corrupt input have not been checked against original samples, and a working decoder is not proof of every original rule.
After expanding, each archive starts with a little-endian 16-bit count, then a table of offsets from the start of the expanded data. A zero offset means an empty slot.

blocks.text: The first record always sits right after the table, at 2 + entry size × entries; for ordinary pictures that is 2 + 4 × count. The build recomputes the fixed archives' offsets and checks each against the rules:
Each record starts with a 16-bit width and a 16-bit height, then its rows. Ordinary pictures round the stored width up to a multiple of eight:

Don't apply this rounding everywhere: the dungeon, item and monster archives use their dimensions as given. A proportional-font glyph record is 12 bytes: width, height (always 8), then eight row bytes. The space glyph has width zero but still has a record, and a glyph's width is not its text advance.

blocks.caption: 4 bits per pixel: the left pixel is the high nibble.
Masks, 1 bit per pixel: bit 7 is the earliest pixel.

blocks.text: Example bytes for illustration, not taken from the game. In `ITEMS` and `MON` archives each image's mask follows it as its own record. Which mask polarity means "draw", and how opaque black is treated, have not been verified.
The files store palette indexes, not colours. Redux's review exporter maps them to the standard 16-colour EGA palette:

Dungeon combat and the ending change some tiles' colours. Redux's current model swaps palette-index bits 1 and 2 for selected tiles in dungeons and uses a separate lossy mapping for the ending, applied as it draws. The original driver tables are not decoded yet.

`TILES.16` uses the same LZW wrapper but none of the archive layouts above. Tile n starts at byte 128 × n of the expanded data; each row is 4 bits per pixel with the left pixel in the high nibble. The data is the four 16,384-byte source sheets joined in order. The CGA `TILES.4` expands to 32,768 bytes, 64 per tile.

items: Plot the current point using the previous command's pen state, then move.

A zero byte ends a segment. Startup draws four segments, starting at (44,68), (64,94), (143,78) and (167,105).
